Police Failures

By: Catherine Rice | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Three children are murdered every day in South Africa.

Unique Selling Point:
Three children are murdered in South Africa every day. In the most recent crime statistics, released in August, it was revealed that 293 children were murdered between April and June this year - fifty more children than in the same period last year. It's a twenty percent increase, and shockingly many of these cases are unresolved.

Summary:
Four year old Mia Botha went missing on Sunday, the 25th of September last year. The community of Klein Nederberg in Paarl East in the Western Cape watches out for all the children in the area. But, on that day, nobody was witness to her abduction. Her body was found the next day in an open field next to a school close to her home. Plastic had been shoved into her mouth, and she had been placed in a bag. Two suspects were arrested shortly afterwards, but were both released because of a lack of evidence. It's been almost a year since then and the case remains unsolved. in a strikingly similar case, four year old Bogkabo Poo went missing in Benoni in October last year. Residents later discovered parts of her mutilated body. Ntokozo Zikhali, who was out on bail at the time for raping a nine year old girl, was arrested. But, last month he was acquitted by the Pretoria High Court which ruled his confession had not been taken correctly, that proper procedure had not been followed.

Further information:
In both cases, there have been no further arrests, and the cases remain unsolved. In a recent parliamentary reply National Police Commissioner Bheki Cele revealed detective shortages across the country. The detective deficit stands at just over 25% in the Western Cape. The worst affected province in the country is the North West with a 32% shortage. Police officers who have left SAPS say the rot started under Jackie Selebi and the closing down of specialised units in the early 2000s.

Script:


VO 1 Two four year old girls…. Both brutally murdered. Their mothers separated by province…but joined in loss. In both cases, police fail to catch their killers. What lies behind the failure of detectives to get justice?

VO 2 It’s a Monday afternoon … four year old Bokgabo Poo is playing in the Wattville neighbourhood park…The date is October 10th, almost exactly a year ago.

VO 3 Here in Benoni South on Johannesburg’s East Rand, children play in the streets.

VO 4 It’s a tightknit community.

VO 5 Bokgabo’s mother is out for most of the day, but when she returns a nightmare that will never end…begins.

UPSOUND Tsholofelo Poo / Bokgabo’s mother 06:08 I got a call to say we can’t find Bokgabo anywhere.

VO 6 Tsholofelo rushes to the park - there’s no sign of her daughter.

VO 7 She tries the home of Bokgabo’s friend, a five year old boy.

UPSOUND Tsholofelo Poo It was 8 o’clock and I asked Sihle where is Bokgabo. That’s when Sihle explained there was a man who came to us and he gave me R2 and ordered me to go buy lollipops at Thomas - the furthest shop from the park.

VO 8 Tsholofelo knows that every second counts….she needs the police’s help.

UPSOUND Tsholofelo Poo / Bokgabo’s mother 15:20 At the police station, they had said, there are no vans there and they're still waiting for it to come through and that time what puzzles us there were that four police vans were there with flat tyres at the police station - just flat tyres.

VO 9 Without police help, Tsholofelo tries the tavern close to the park which has CCTV cameras. But, its late…and the owner turns her away….insisting she comes back the next day.

UPSOUND Tsholofelo Poo The community, I remember, they were literally trying to bring the gate down because everyone was like there is a child missing. 21:11 I had no tears at that time. There was no time to cry. Because all that was resting in my head was this is a puzzle I need to solve.

VO 10 Its morning by the time she is finally able to access the CCTV footage…now, with police detectives….

VO 11 A man, later identified as Ntokozo Zikhali…walking with her beloved Bokgabo.

VO 12 The little girl skipping happily.

VO 13 But, the evidence comes too late…within hours, Tsholofelo would be told that a child’s body part has been discovered, buried in the yard of a house not far away… the resident made the discovery while sweeping her yard. Tsholofelo is able to see it through the fence.

VO 14 Soon after, children playing in an open field find a torso – and call police.

UPSOUND Tsholofelo Poo They explained they’re going to show me a picture of the t-shirt on the phone. When he showed me the t-shirt, I identified it as belonging to Bokgabo.

VO 15 Days later, police arrest Ntokozo Zikhali.

PRESENTER LINK Shockingly, at the time of the murder Zikhali was out on bail for raping a nine year old girl.

VO 16 Now police charge him with kidnapping, murder, defeating the ends of justice and the violation of a corpse.

VO 17 But, it seems in their haste, under pressure to make an arrest…police may have taken things too far.

VO 18 Procedure is not followed and Zikhali’s confession is ruled inadmissible in court after he claims it had been beaten out of him.

VO 19 The CCTV footage is found insufficient to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt.

VO 20 Last month, he’s acquitted of Bokgabo’s murder.

UPSOUND Tsholofelo Poo 1:04:35 You’re saying Notokozo is not related to anything that happened to Bokgabo then who else is? The last time I spoke to the police was on the 10th of August, and that’s because the community had marched to court. They said they are assigning five detectives, but till this day I haven’t heard anything from them.

VO 21 Zikhali is serving a life sentence in the other case for raping a nine year old girl. To date nobody has been arrested for Bokgabo’s murder.

PRESENTER LINK When children are murdered and their killers walk away scot free, families are left with little closure and some out of sheer desperation are turning to non profits to pick up the pieces where police have left off.

VO 22 Kobie, who asked us to hide his identity, is a private investigator, hired by civil rights organisation Action Society to strengthen the police investigation.

VO 23 He’s spent hours combing the area for witnesses in the search for Bokgabo’s killer.

UPSOUND Kobie / Private Investigator If you look at the first crime to the second crime, he’s a child molestor, not a person who cuts up children. From the time she went missing to the next morning, she was mutilated and in pieces, half the body was not found. So, there has to be somebody different in charge or possibly involved where he brought the child to.

VO 24 In other words, could it be more sinister than it first appeared… that some mastermind orchestrated the abduction.

VO 25 For Kobie, Bokgabo’s case shows how police should approach reports of missing children…with urgency.

UPSOUND Kobie / Private investigator FX_5629.MXF 01:34 You have to react immediately. Missing children have to be treated as an emergency. There’s not that thing of 24 hours whatever. Its critical to follow up immediately.

PRESENTER LINK You would expect the investigation of child murders would be a top police priority with DNA evidence fasttracked and experienced detectives on these cases, so why isn’t this happening?

VO 26 Kobie has seen that the failure in Bokgabo’s case is down to a shortage of competent police detectives.

VO 27 A committed investigator would bring the family closure and restore the community’s sense of security.

UPSOUND Kobie There’s somebody out there cutting up people badly, and that must be stopped.

VO 28 For Tsholofelo each day tears her further away from her daughter.

UPSOUND Tsholofelo Poo I’m the walking dead. This is the first time I’m going to reveal this that there isn’t a day I don’t go without drinking. When its time to go to sleep you need that hard kick, so that it does not come to your dreams. Because the image I saw, no woman deserves to see that, what I saw.

VO 29 If there’s ever to be justice for her child – it will have to come from decent policing.

VO 30 A former police officer who we’ll call Bill, spent 30 years in the service.

VO 31 Bill didn’t want to be identified – but believes the decline in policing standards started more than two decades ago.

PRESENTER: Why do you think things have gone so wrong?

UPSOUND Bill /Former Police officer This is a structural problem top down. Competence and ability cannot be sacrificed and that currently is the biggest problem.

VO 32 He feels that junior detectives are not getting the guidance and training they need.

UPSOUND “Bill” / former police officer You can’t just grab the guy and say he did it. You still need to connect all the dots and all the elements of that crime and being able to present it in court and that is where we have the problem.

VO 33 Faith in the police and justice system to deal with child killers has dwindled…not just in Gauteng where collection of evidence failed in this case.

VO 34 …but also the processing of vital evidence to help identify killers.

VO 35 …Udene Botha’s four year old daughter, Tamia, was murdered just a few weeks before Bokgabo.

VO 36 Paarl: home of wine farms and majestic mountains.

VO37 …But a dark underbelly of violent crime simmers beneath the pretty veneer. …. Particularly in Klein Nederberg in Paarl East.

VO 38… Where gangsterism is rife, poverty and unemployment are everywhere.

VO 39 Everyone called Udene’s little girl Mia. They lived in a busy spot near a soup kitchen… and a park where she used to play.

VO 40 Udene remembers every detail of Septermber 25th when Mia disappeared.

UPSOUND FX6 - 5601.MXF Day One / Udene Botha / Mia’s mother 04:38 Sy was nie in loadshedding gevat nie. Dit was sommer mevrou. En dit was lig en dit was warm and almal het buite gespeel.

UPSOUND Udene Botha 08:24 Udene Botha / Mother Ek vra waar is Mia, en niemand hulle weet nie waar Mia is nie, maar almal se Mia het hier in die rondte gespeel.

VO 41 That night, Udene scarcely slept.

VO 42 The following day, the community discovered Mia’s body on the field of the primary school – stuffed into a black bag by her killer.

UPSOUND Udene Botha / Mia’s mother 14:57 Sy was nie ‘n dier nie.

VO 43 With little police response in the moment, the community raged…taking revenge into their own hands.

UPSOUND Kaylynn Palm / Action Society (Day one FX6_5602) 05:03 The community was very angry, they thought one guy was the killer and they allegedly killed him with a panga. Following that, two more people were arrested, but days later were released. .

VO 44 Action Society deployed Kaylynn Palm to try and source information on the police investigation - and she’s become Mia's family’s only source of comfort….we meet on a bleak, Cape winter’s day.

UPSOUND Kaylynn Palm / Action Society 06:16 The concerning bit is different officers come to Mia’s mom and each one tells a different story. There are so many stories you’re not getting proper feedback. We have written letters, but zero feedback.

VO 45 Former police officer Bill believes this is happening in many cases across the country….and has been for years now… Under a previous national police commissioner specialised policing units were disbanded in the early 2000s.

UPSOUND Bill / Former police officer We destroyed a lot in the police service that you cannot just rebuild by establishing another unit.

PRESENTER: I’m afraid to say some police stations you go into you can hardly find a pen.

UPSOUND Bill I have taken pen and paper to a police station not far from where we are writing my statements myself, not even a chair to sit on.

VO 46 As the anniversary of Mia’s murder approached, we asked police what’s going on with their investigation - they wrote that “DNA samples are being processed, and the case remains a priority”.

ON SCREEN: “Kindly be advised that all DNA samples are being processed. The mentioned case was prioritised and the investigator is awaiting the results.”

UPSOUND Kaylynn Palm / Action Society “If child murders were a priority, we wouldn’t have close to three hundred children dying in a three month period. Time after time we are in court. We are seeing this week after week. The system is failing them.

VO 47 Udene lives with endless questions that only a committed detective can answer.

UPSOUND Udene Botha They didn’t rape her. Hulle het haar versmoor. I don’t know why.

NATSOUND Singing

VO48 Udene would sing Mia to sleep with church songs.

VO 49 The school field where her little body was found…

VO 50 …echoes with the sounds of children playing.

NATSOUND Children playing on the field

UPSOUND ERIN If you could give a message to police minister about your family, your daughter and the case, what would you say to Bheki Cele?

UPSOUND Udene Ek wil se volgens my het die polisie niks gedoen nie. 24:57 Mia must get justice, it's not right and I will never forgive whoever did this.

VO 51 Both Bokgabo Poo and Mia Botha were snatched in broad daylight by criminals who clearly had little fear of being caught or punished.

VO 52 Bill / Former police officer From the criminals side, they don’t fear the police, and I don’t say fear because they are using violence, they fear them because they are effective ..ERIN: and sophisticated… BILL: that you will fear. If you know what you’re doing the criminals will fear you, but if you don’t, they know you’re not going to build this case against them, and they going to outplay you in court.

VO 34 …but also the processing of vital evidence to help identify killers. VO 35 …Udene Botha’s four year old daughter, Tamia, was murdered just a few weeks before Bokgabo. VO 36 Paarl: home of wine farms and majestic mountains. VO37 …But a dark underbelly of violent crime simmers beneath the pretty veneer. …. Particularly in Klein Nederberg in Paarl East. VO 38… Where gangsterism is rife, poverty and unemployment are everywhere. VO 39 Everyone called Udene’s little girl Mia. They lived in a busy spot near a soup kitchen… and a park where she used to play. VO 40 Udene remembers every detail of Septermber 25th when Mia disappeared. UPSOUND FX6 - 5601.MXF Day One / Udene Botha / Mia’s mother 04:38 Sy was nie in loadshedding gevat nie. Dit was sommer mevrou. En dit was lig en dit was warm and almal het buite gespeel. UPSOUND Udene Botha 08:24 Udene Botha / Mother Ek vra waar is Mia, en niemand hulle weet nie waar Mia is nie, maar almal se Mia het hier in die rondte gespeel. VO 41 That night, Udene scarcely slept. VO 42 The following day, the community discovered Mia’s body on the field of the primary school – stuffed into a black bag by her killer. UPSOUND Udene Botha / Mia’s mother 14:57 Sy was nie ‘n dier nie. VO 43 With little police response in the moment, the community raged…taking revenge into their own hands. UPSOUND Kaylynn Palm / Action Society (Day one FX6_5602) 05:03 The community was very angry, they thought one guy was the killer and they allegedly killed him with a panga. Following that, two more people were arrested, but days later were released. . VO 44 Action Society deployed Kaylynn Palm to try and source information on the police investigation - and she’s become Mia's family’s only source of comfort….we meet on a bleak, Cape winter’s day. UPSOUND Kaylynn Palm / Action Society 06:16 The concerning bit is different officers come to Mia’s mom and each one tells a different story. There are so many stories you’re not getting proper feedback. We have written letters, but zero feedback. VO 45 Former police officer Bill believes this is happening in many cases across the country….and has been for years now… Under a previous national police commissioner specialised policing units were disbanded in the early 2000s. UPSOUND Bill / Former police officer We destroyed a lot in the police service that you cannot just rebuild by establishing another unit. PRESENTER: I’m afraid to say some police stations you go into you can hardly find a pen. UPSOUND Bill I have taken pen and paper to a police station not far from where we are writing my statements myself, not even a chair to sit on. VO 46 As the anniversary of Mia’s murder approached, we asked police what’s going on with their investigation - they wrote that “DNA samples are being processed, and the case remains a priority”. ON SCREEN: “Kindly be advised that all DNA samples are being processed. The mentioned case was prioritised and the investigator is awaiting the results.” UPSOUND Kaylynn Palm / Action Society “If child murders were a priority, we wouldn’t have close to three hundred children dying in a three month period. Time after time we are in court. We are seeing this week after week. The system is failing them. VO 47 Udene lives with endless questions that only a committed detective can answer. UPSOUND Udene Botha They didn’t rape her. Hulle het haar versmoor. I don’t know why. NATSOUND Singing VO48 Udene would sing Mia to sleep with church songs. VO 49 The school field where her little body was found… VO 50 …echoes with the sounds of children playing. NATSOUND Children playing on the field UPSOUND ERIN If you could give a message to police minister about your family, your daughter and the case, what would you say to Bheki Cele? UPSOUND Udene Ek wil se volgens my het die polisie niks gedoen nie. 24:57 Mia must get justice, it's not right and I will never forgive whoever did this. VO 51 Both Bokgabo Poo and Mia Botha were snatched in broad daylight by criminals who clearly had little fear of being caught or punished. VO 52 Bill / Former police officer From the criminals side, they don’t fear the police, and I don’t say fear because they are using violence, they fear them because they are effective ..ERIN: and sophisticated… BILL: that you will fear. If you know what you’re doing the criminals will fear you, but if you don’t, they know you’re not going to build this case against them, and they going to outplay you in court.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Three children are murdered every day in South Africa.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Three children are murdered in South Africa every day. In the most recent crime statistics, released in August, it was revealed that 293 children were murdered between April and June this year - fifty more children than in the same period last year. It's a twenty percent increase, and shockingly many of these cases are unresolved.
metadata.Summary: Four year old Mia Botha went missing on Sunday, the 25th of September last year. The community of Klein Nederberg in Paarl East in the Western Cape watches out for all the children in the area. But, on that day, nobody was witness to her abduction. Her body was found the next day in an open field next to a school close to her home. Plastic had been shoved into her mouth, and she had been placed in a bag. Two suspects were arrested shortly afterwards, but were both released because of a lack of evidence. It's been almost a year since then and the case remains unsolved. in a strikingly similar case, four year old Bogkabo Poo went missing in Benoni in October last year. Residents later discovered parts of her mutilated body. Ntokozo Zikhali, who was out on bail at the time for raping a nine year old girl, was arrested. But, last month he was acquitted by the Pretoria High Court which ruled his confession had not been taken correctly, that proper procedure had not been followed.
metadata.Further information: In both cases, there have been no further arrests, and the cases remain unsolved. In a recent parliamentary reply National Police Commissioner Bheki Cele revealed detective shortages across the country. The detective deficit stands at just over 25% in the Western Cape. The worst affected province in the country is the North West with a 32% shortage. Police officers who have left SAPS say the rot started under Jackie Selebi and the closing down of specialised units in the early 2000s.
